top_signal.title: How are startups handling WhatsApp when the conversations involve serious money?
top_signal.summary: We’re a startup so naturally half the company runs through WhatsApp lol. It’s quick and our customers already use it. The problem is we deal with high-end clients and some pretty high-value transactions. That makes me nervous about how much trust we put in a WhatsApp account. If a client’s account gets compromised and we get a message changing payment details or approving something sensitive how are we supposed to know it’s actually them? We’ve looked at separate callbacks and verification through known contacts. I saw kibu while looking into this which takes the approach of establishing a trusted connection with the actual person and verifying them again when needed. There seem to be other identity and verification tools trying to solve parts of this too. I don’t really want to replace WhatsApp because that’s where people already are. I’m more interested in having a separate verification layer for the few requests where getting it wrong could cost a lot. I wanna know what everyone thinks or any piece of advice will be super helpful.       submitted by     /u/troubledhorror       [link]       [comments]
